paragraphs: Here's my big idea, friend: God's mercy is bigger than our mess, and our mess is still our mess. Israel kept walking in Jeroboam's sins, and Aram kept crushing them, and that's the whole sad loop (2 Kings 13:2-3). But when King Jehoahaz sought the favor of the LORD, "the LORD listened to him because He saw the oppression that the king of Aram had inflicted on Israel" (2 Kings 13:4). Then the LORD gave Israel a deliverer, even though they went right back to those same sins (2 Kings 13:5-6). The mercy didn't come because they earned it, and that gives me hope.

Now look at the end of the chapter. "The LORD was gracious to Israel and had compassion on them, and He turned toward them because of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob" (2 Kings 13:23). That's the reason the text gives, and it's a promise God made, not a promise Israel kept. He keeps His word even when His people don't keep theirs. That's the kind of God you can run back to, no matter how long you've been wandering.

But here's the other half, and I'll say it gently. King Jehoash struck the ground three times and stopped, and Elisha told him he should have struck it five or six times (2 Kings 13:18-19). God had promised victory, and the king still quit early. I know that feeling, friend, because I've called a batch finished when I was only halfway there. So when God hands you something, don't settle for the minimum. Take it all the way, with a full heart, and keep striking that ground.
